questions.q: What is the main difference between a 'snack' and a 'main meal'?
options: Snacks are heavy meals eaten three times a day, while main meals are eaten once.
A snack is a small, light portion of food typically eaten between meals, whereas a main meal is larger and more balanced.
Snacks are always liquid drinks, and main meals are solid foods.
A main meal requires no cooking, but a snack takes hours to prepare.
questions.explain: A main meal (like lunch or dinner) provides a substantial amount of balanced nutrients meant to sustain the body, while a snack is a smaller food portion eaten temporarily to satisfy hunger between meals.

questions.q: Which of the following items are classic examples of common snacks available in Nigerian society?
options: Pounded yam and Egusi soup
Fufu and bitterleaf soup
Chin-chin, puff-puff, and roasted plantain (Boli)
Jollof rice and fried turkey
questions.explain: Chin-chin, puff-puff, and roasted plantain (boli) are very common light foods or 'snacks' eaten to tide over hunger in Nigeria, as opposed to heavy swallows and rice dishes which are main meals.

questions.q: Which of the following popular local beverages (drinks) is commonly prepared and marketed in society?
options: Zobo and Kunu
Imported apple cider
Aged French wine
Carbonated energy drinks only
questions.explain: Zobo (made from hibiscus leaves) and Kunu (made from millet or sorghum) are highly popular, nutritious local drinks prepared and sold across society.

questions.q: In the preparation of the local 'Zobo' drink, what is the primary raw material used?
options: Fermented maize grain
Roasted coffee beans
Squeezed orange peels
Dried roselle (hibiscus) leaves
questions.explain: Zobo is traditionally prepared by boiling the dried dark-red calyces of the Roselle plant (Hibiscus sabdariffa) along with spices like ginger and cloves.

questions.q: What is a major duty of a commercial food seller or provider to the public?
options: To secretly sell expired ingredients to avoid financial loss.
To prepare and serve wholesome, hygienic, and safe food in a clean environment.
To force people to consume food they are allergic to.
To display dirty utensils to show hard work.
questions.explain: Food sellers owe a duty of care to the public to ensure that all meals are prepared under strictly hygienic conditions to prevent disease outbreaks and food poisoning.

questions.q: Why is it a standard hygienic and legal rule for public food handlers to undergo regular medical check-ups?
options: To ensure they eat enough to gain weight.
To identify and treat communicable diseases like typhoid or tuberculosis so they don't infect the consumers.
To qualify them for free housing benefits.
To prove that they can lift heavy pots.
questions.explain: Regular health screenings are vital to certify that food handlers do not carry contagious diseases (such as typhoid, hepatitis A, or tuberculosis) that can be easily transferred to consumers through food.

questions.q: When preparing popular local snacks like 'Puff-puff' or 'Akara', which primary cooking method is used?
options: Steaming
Deep frying
Grilling
Boiling
questions.explain: Puff-puff (sweet dough) and Akara (bean paste) are both cooked by totally immersing them in a deep pan of hot vegetable or palm oil, a process known as deep frying.

questions.q: Why is it important to properly cool freshly cooked meals or baked snacks before sealing them in plastic packaging?
options: To make the food completely tasteless and hard.
To ensure the plastic permanently melts onto the food for security.
To stop condensation (steam) from trapping moisture inside, which would cause sogginess and rapid spoilage.
To dramatically change the original color of the food.
questions.explain: Sealing hot food in a container creates steam (condensation), resulting in a damp environment that ruins the texture of the food and encourages the rapid growth of bacteria and mold.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary reasons for packaging processed food?
options: To hide the true quality of the product and make it heavier.
To protect the food from contamination, preserve its shelf life, and provide a surface for product labeling.
To allow easy access for household pests.
To ensure the food absorbs moisture from the atmosphere.
questions.explain: Packaging serves protective functions (against germs, dirt, and damage), preserves freshness, and acts as a medium to communicate essential information (ingredients, expiry date) to buyers.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a safe, environmentally friendly packaging material for wrapping local foods like 'Moi-Moi'?
options: Heavy-duty industrial nylon bags
Lead-based metallic containers
Broad plantain or banana leaves (Uma leaves)
Non-biodegradable styrofoam packs
questions.explain: Broad plantain or 'Uma' leaves are natural, biodegradable, non-toxic packaging materials traditionally used to wrap and steam foods like Moi-Moi, often imparting a desirable flavor.

questions.q: The core marketing principles are often summarized in business as the '4 Ps'. Which of the following correctly identifies these four principles?
options: Package, Preserve, Process, Produce
People, Power, Paper, Pencil
Product, Price, Place, Promotion
Pan, Pot, Plate, Platter
questions.explain: The standard marketing mix (the 4 Ps) consists of the Product (what is sold), Price (how much it costs), Place (where it is sold), and Promotion (how it is advertised).

questions.q: In the marketing of food, what does the principle of 'Pricing' heavily rely on?
options: Randomly guessing how much a customer has in their pocket.
Calculating the total cost of raw materials, preparation, packaging, and desired profit.
Giving the food away for free to gain popularity.
Only looking at the visual appearance of the food.
questions.explain: Pricing a product effectively requires calculating the production costs (ingredients, labor, packaging, fuel) and adding a reasonable markup for profit so the business can sustain itself.

options: Promotion
Product formulation
Pricing
Placement
questions.explain: Promotion involves all advertising and communication strategies used to raise awareness about a product, inform consumers of its benefits, and encourage them to make a purchase.

questions.q: When a food seller displays freshly baked snacks inside a clean, well-lit transparent glass case, what dual purpose is achieved?
options: It hides the food and makes the glass dirty.
It attracts buyers through visual appeal while protecting the food from dust, flies, and sneezing.
It rapidly decreases the nutritional value of the snack due to the light.
It stops the seller from having to talk to the consumer.
questions.explain: A transparent showcase serves a promotional purpose by displaying the attractive product to potential customers, while simultaneously acting as a hygienic barrier against environmental contaminants.

questions.q: Including a clear label on packaged food stating 'Contains Peanuts' satisfies which vital duty of the food provider?
options: The duty to enforce government taxation.
The duty to warn consumers and protect them from potentially fatal food allergies.
The duty to increase the physical weight of the product.
The duty to make the package design harder to read.
questions.explain: Food providers have a strict duty of care to provide accurate ingredient information, especially regarding common allergens like peanuts, which could trigger life-threatening reactions in susceptible consumers.

questions.q: A standard packaged food label is legally required by regulatory bodies to display which of the following vital pieces of information?
options: The manufacturer's daily profit margin.
The full recipe and exact cooking secrets of the company.
The list of ingredients, nutritional information, and best-before (expiry) date.
The private phone numbers of the factory workers.
questions.explain: Food packaging must transparently inform consumers about what is inside the food (ingredients/allergens), its nutritional value, and how long it remains safe to eat (expiry date).
